When Sikhī, the Lord of the World, the best among speakers, had attained Nibbāna,
I was joyful with a joyful heart.
I worshipped that supreme stupa.
Having had it repaired by craftsmen and having given them the payment at that time, I—
Joyful with a joyful heart,
I had a sacrificial offering made.
For eight eons among the devas,
In some aeons I dwelt continuously;
in the remaining aeons,
I wandered through various births.
Poison does not affect my body,
nor do weapons strike me down;
I do not die by water.
This is the fruit of the sacrifice:
whatever rain I desire,
the great cloud pours down.
Even the gods come under my control;
this is the fruit of meritorious deeds.
Endowed with the seven treasures—
Thirty times I was a king;
no one ever despised me—
this is the fruit of meritorious karma.
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
I had a sacrificial altar made with twin pillars;
I do not recall ever being born in an unhappy state.
This is the fruit of making an offering:
the four analytical knowledges (*paṭisambhidā*), and so forth...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Āyāgadāyaka recited these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Āyāgadāyaka.
